title: What If NASA Taped Over the Moon Landing? It Did

scenes.text: What if NASA taped over the first Moon landing? It did, to save on tape.
In 1969 the Moon camera sent a format TV couldn't show. Converting it for broadcast left the picture badly degraded.
The sharper originals were stored at NASA on 45 reels of data tape.
Then, in the 1970s and 80s, a tape shortage hit. NASA erased and reused about 200,000 tapes.
A three-year search ended in 2009: the Moon reels were almost certainly among them.
So NASA paid a film restoration company 230,000 dollars to clean up copies saved by TV networks. The best footage of the landing is a copy.

description:
What if NASA taped over the first Moon landing? In July 2009 the agency admitted it almost certainly had.
Apollo 11's camera sent its picture in a format ordinary television could not show, and the conversion for broadcast degraded it; the better original signal was recorded on 45 reels of data tape. During a tape shortage in the 1970s and 80s NASA pulled, erased and reused about 200,000 tapes, and after a three-year search engineers concluded the Apollo 11 reels were among them. NASA then paid Lowry Digital about 230,000 dollars to restore the moonwalk from broadcast copies, including tapes kept by CBS.
What should we run through next?
